evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: Aggression was observed equally in male and female patients (8 patients, out of 22 individuals in the replication cohort).

evidence.reference_title: Lrrc7 mutant mice model developmental emotional dysregulation that can be alleviated by mGluR5 allosteric modulation.
evidence.snippet: Consistent with a critical role of LRRC7 in emotional regulation, mutant mice had inappropriate juvenile aggressive behavior and significant anxiety-like behavior and social dysfunction in adulthood.

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: two independent studies on Lrrc7 deficient mice have observed a strong aggression phenotype in homozygous, but also in male heterozygous ko mice

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: Four patients with truncating variants in the central part of the mRNA/protein (exons 20/21) showed hyperphagia due to reduced satiety, leading to class II obesity in three of them.

nodes.description: Missense variants cluster in the N-terminal leucine-rich repeat (LRR) domain at conserved consensus positions (L65, N94, C106, L296), and these abolish LRR binding to protein phosphatase 1 alpha, MACF1 and Erbin in 293T cells. L296P also prevents postsynaptic targeting. The PDZ-domain variant L1567Q reduces delta-catenin binding and the fraction of densin-180 clusters at Shank3-positive synapses.

evidence.snippet: In summary, four variants at key positions of the LRR consensus sequence (L65, N94, C106 and L296) severely disrupt binding to all partners tested.

nodes.description: Hyperphagia from reduced satiety, beginning between 4 and 10 years of age and resembling Prader-Willi syndrome food-seeking, was seen in 4 of 14 individuals with truncating variants, all with variants in exons 20/21. Several others were too young to assess.

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: Hyperphagia was observed in 4 out of 14 cases with truncating variants described in Supplemental Data 1; however, several of the other patients were still too young to observe this phenotype and a follow up will be needed later in life.

nodes.description: Densin-null mice lose mGluR- and NMDA receptor-dependent long-term depression. LTD requires densin-180, PP1 activity and CaMKII, and is the plasticity defect the defining study links to intellectual disability.

evidence.reference_title: Deletion of densin-180 results in abnormal behaviors associated with mental illness and reduces mGluR5 and DISC1 in the postsynaptic density fraction.
evidence.snippet: In addition, deletion of densin results in impairment of mGluR- and NMDA receptor-dependent forms of long-term depression

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: Phenotypic analysis using human phenotype ontology (HPO) terms found that in addition to ID (81%), the affected individuals with pLoF LRRC7 variants displayed neurodevelopmental delay (84%), delayed development of speech (81%), delayed motor development (45%) and global developmental delay (30%)

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: Out of the 42 genes associated with this class, LRRC7 ranked 19th, with a PPA almost equal to 1

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that LRRC7 encodes a major determinant of intellectual development and behaviour.

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: In at least eleven cases where both parents were available for analysis, we determined that the respective variant appeared de novo.

nodes.description: More than half of affected individuals carry nonsense, splice-site or frameshift variants, or a deletion of the last exon, expected to undergo nonsense-mediated decay. Together with strong population constraint on LRRC7 (pLI = 1), this points to haploinsufficiency of densin-180 as the main mechanism.

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: This suggests haploinsufficiency for the encoded Densin-180 protein as a major pathomechanism, consistent with human population data from gnomAD (pLI = 1, o/e = 0.13, gnomAD v4.1.0).

nodes.description: Densin-180 binds the alpha subunit of CaMKII through central and C-terminal sites and PP1 alpha through its LRR, and can bridge them into a CaMKII/densin-180/PP1 complex. Loss of this scaffold is proposed to mistarget PP1 and alter dephosphorylation of CaMKII and other synaptic substrates during plasticity; densin-null neurons show altered early regulation of CaMKII by NMDA receptors.

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: These data are compatible with a model where Densin-180 may scaffold a αCaMKII/Densin-180/PP1α triple complex.

evidence.reference_title: Variants in LRRC7 lead to intellectual disability, autism, aggression and abnormal eating behaviors.
evidence.snippet: αCaMKII phosphorylation at Thr286 upon stimulation of NMDA receptors is higher in neurons derived from Lrrc7 ko mice compared to WT

nodes.description: Homozygous null mice show behaviours considered endophenotypes of autism and schizophrenia, reduced postsynaptic mGluR5 and DISC1, impaired mGluR- and NMDA receptor-dependent LTD, altered CaMKII regulation and changed spine morphology.
Homozygous mutants show juvenile aggression, adult anxiety-like behaviour and social dysfunction, and impaired neurite outgrowth; all were improved by the mGluR5 positive allosteric modulator CDPPB.

nodes.description: Patient LRR variants reduce dendritic branching of cultured hippocampal neurons, and neurons from Lrrc7 mutant mice have impaired neurite outgrowth.

evidence.reference_title: Lrrc7 mutant mice model developmental emotional dysregulation that can be alleviated by mGluR5 allosteric modulation.
evidence.snippet: Furthermore, mutant primary neurons had impaired neurite outgrowth which was rescued by CDPPB treatment.

nodes.description: Densin-180 binds the Cav1.2 N-terminus and promotes forward trafficking and dendritic clustering of Cav1.2 L-type channels. Densin-null neurons have lower surface Cav1.2, current density and excitation-transcription signaling.

evidence.reference_title: Densin-180 Controls the Trafficking and Signaling of L-Type Voltage-Gated Ca(v)1.2 Ca(2+) Channels at Excitatory Synapses.
evidence.snippet: We conclude that densin is an essential regulator of neuronal Cav1 channels and ensures efficient Cav1.2 Ca2+ signaling at excitatory synapses.

nodes.description: Densin-180 loss selectively reduces mGluR5 (and DISC1) in the postsynaptic density fraction while leaving ionotropic glutamate receptors unchanged.

biological_processes: mGluR5 localization to the postsynaptic density

evidence.reference_title: Deletion of densin-180 results in abnormal behaviors associated with mental illness and reduces mGluR5 and DISC1 in the postsynaptic density fraction.
evidence.snippet: These results indicate that densin influences the function of mGluRs and CaMKII at synapses and contributes to localization of mGluR5 and DISC1 in the PSD fraction.
